title: Best Cordless Vacuum Cleaners UK
short: Cordless stick vacuums compared by runtime, weight, bin size and who they suit.
intro: Cordless vacuums have largely replaced corded uprights in UK homes. This guide compares the models Expert Reviews picked from its testing, from premium Dynsons to budget and self-emptying options, so you can match the machine to your floors and budget.

products.name: V15 Detect Absolute
products.best_for: Buyers who want premium cleaning power and smart features
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall winner. It has superb cleaning power, a laser that reveals fine dust and a strong battery, but it is heavy and expensive and does not empty itself.
products.search: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute cordless vacuum

products.name: Cyclone V10
products.best_for: Buyers who want Dyson performance at a lower price than the V15
products.summary: A lighter, cheaper Dyson with excellent cleaning power and good battery life, though it is still expensive next to non-Dyson rivals.

products.name: V15s Detect Submarine
products.best_for: Buyers who want to vacuum and mop hard floors with one machine
products.summary: A cordless Dyson that vacuums and mops. It is powerful, but Expert Reviews notes it is expensive and the Submarine head needs substantial maintenance.
pros: Versatile vacuum and mop in one

products.name: PowerDetect IP3251UKT
products.best_for: People who want to empty the bin as rarely as possible
products.summary: A cordless vacuum with a self-emptying base station and competitive cleaning performance, and a long runtime, though it can feel stiff on some carpets.
cons: Stiff movement on some carpet types

products.name: IZ300UKT
products.summary: A cordless Shark with a dual-roller DuoClean head that copes well with controlled spills on hard floors, though it is heavy.
cons: Vacuum lifts when pulled backwards on carpet

products.name: ICZ300UKT
products.best_for: Buyers who want a stand-alone upright and strong suction
products.summary: An upright-style cordless that stands on its own and has powerful suction. Expert Reviews found it difficult to assemble and weaker in corners.

products.name: Quick
products.best_for: Long cleaning sessions and people who prefer bags to bins
products.summary: A bagged cordless with large dust bags and easy emptying, and good cleaning performance overall, though it has no anti-tangle head and weaker suction than rivals.

products.name: HF9
products.summary: A cheap cordless with solid cleaning performance that stands upright. It has a short runtime, no eco mode and no soft roller for hard floors.
cons: No soft roller for hard floors

guide.q: What runtime do I need from a cordless vacuum?
guide.a: Check the quoted runtime on the mode you will actually use. Maximum power runs the battery down much faster than the standard mode. For a small flat, around 30 minutes may be enough. Larger homes benefit from 60 minutes or more.
Bins are cheaper to run and easier to empty into a bin bag, but can release dust. Bagged models like the Henry Quick keep dust contained and can be more hygienic to empty, at the cost of buying bags.

They move dust into a larger bag or bin so you empty it only every few weeks. They cost more and need space near a socket, but they make cleaning far less of a chore, especially for allergy sufferers.
Weight matters most if you will lift the machine to clean stairs or ceilings. The models here range from about 2.7kg to over 6kg, so try to pick the lightest one that meets your cleaning needs.
